The problem

What the field had — and what it needed

For three years, above-store leaders had no single source of truth for training status. Data was assembled manually, arrived secondhand, and surfaced problems only after they had grown.

What this project was — and was not
A dashboard configuration task
A report request handed to an analyst
A plug-and-play LMS feature
A full-stack data product built solo
A BI architecture designed from scratch
A change management system for adoption
Before
  • Manually collecting AD updates weekly
  • Piecing together spreadsheets by region
  • Relying on secondhand store reports
  • No certification expiration visibility
  • No MIT pipeline data in one view
  • Problems surfaced only after they grew
After
  • Data pulled daily from BoUniversity (Docebo)
  • Role-scoped views auto-filter on login
  • Color-coded signals at a glance
  • ServSafe expiration countdown per leader
  • MIT on-track status with weekly resolution
  • Coaching tool — not a reporting burden
System design

Two curated views of the same infrastructure

The eight trackers share a common dashboard structure built in Amazon QuickSight and embedded inside BoUniversity (Docebo). What changes between views is data scope and drill-down depth — curated intentionally for each audience.

Above-store leader view
OpCo Training Tracker: Above Store Level
Regional visibility with drill-down from region → area → store → individual learner.
  • Color-coded area and region completion summaries
  • Expandable rows to store and learner level
  • Scoped to VP, RDO, RTM, and AD audiences
  • Designed for coaching conversations and call prep
Store-level view
OpCo Training Tracker: Store Level
Same eight-tab structure — curated to show only the logged-in leader's store data.
  • Store-scoped completion percentages per course
  • No regional or cross-area data visible
  • Scoped to MIC and GM audiences
  • Designed for daily team follow-up and action
Live system

The dashboards in use

Each tab answers one leadership question. Screenshots show the above-store view — the same trackers appear in the store-level view with scope narrowed to the individual store.

Training Tracker — region and area completion view
Above-store leaders see color-coded completion rates across areas and courses. Green = 80–100%, Yellow = 50–79%, Red = 0–49%. Rows expand from region → area → store → individual learner percentage.
28-Day Tracker — above-store area view
Mandatory onboarding completion by area — expandable from region level. Blank = no enrolled employees.
28-Day Tracker — store-level view
The same tracker, scoped to a single store. MICs and GMs see only their team's completion — no regional data.
Team Trainer Tracker — individual detail
Distinct color logic: green thumbs-up = in role and certified. Red flags surface in-role leaders without completed certification.
ServSafe Certification Status
Days-to/since-expiration per leader. Red = expired, Yellow = within 60 days, Green = 61+ days remaining.
Architecture

Eight trackers, one shared structure

Built in Amazon QuickSight, embedded inside BoUniversity (Docebo). Color thresholds, drill-down depth, and calculated fields are distinct per tracker type.

Training Tracker
Required course completion by region, area, store, and individual learner.
Spanish Course Tracker
Same architecture scoped to Spanish-language course versions with dot-coded progress.
28-Day Onboarding Tracker
Two-panel view: required courses + two-station completion across regions and areas.
Cross-Training Tracker
Station course completion with individual two-station threshold logic per employee.
Team Trainer Tracker
Distinct 0 / 1–99 / 100% color scale. Tracks TT/CTT role-vs-certification alignment.
ServSafe Certification
Days-to/since-expiration logic with area summary rollup and individual detail table.
MIT Tracker
KPI count card + on-track percentage. Week-in-learning-plan logic flags pace gaps.
Leadership Development
Cohort roster view — bench-strength visibility by course, session, and job code.

Readiness infrastructure

Access wasn't enough — adoption required its own layer

A 37-page playbook and 14-slide deck were built alongside the dashboards to move leaders from login to interpretation to repeatable action.

37-Page Readiness Playbook
Login guidance, per-tracker walkthroughs, mastery levels, KPI coaching scripts, AD call structures, resistance-response scripts, and onboarding integration steps.
14-Slide Overview Deck
Above-store leader orientation covering system purpose, access path inside BoUniversity (Docebo), all eight trackers, and how to embed dashboard use in leadership rhythms.
Dashboard Mastery Tracker
Four-level rubric (Exploring → Mastery) for VP/RDO and AD audiences — a shared language for adoption progress over time.
Change Management Design
ADKAR-grounded adoption strategies, reluctant user scripts, and a KPI rotation schedule that embeds dashboard use into existing meeting rhythms.
The written documentation layer
The playbook and deck were designed as a readiness system in their own right — not as afterthoughts. Each piece was written with a distinct audience, entry point, and use case in mind.
Audience
VP of Ops, RDOs, RTMs, ADs — each section speaks to a different role level.
Purpose
Login → navigation → interpretation → coaching action — a full adoption arc.
Design intent
Dashboard access turns into repeatable operating behavior — not one-time exposure.
